question: When the gold Memory does not literally contain the query, does any non-literal candidate generator recall it, and at what candidate-set cost?

decision_relevance.why_now: The completed ordering experiment and its structural follow-up both pin recall of the primary Memory at 1.0 BY CONSTRUCTION. validate_rank_truth (membench/beads_ordering/runner.py:262) raises unless the literal candidate set EQUALS the labelled set, and the authoring path (beads_ordering/corpus.py:600-645) injects the literal query string into exactly the labelled Memories. Verified 36/36 tasks, zero primary misses.
decision_relevance.consequence: Neither experiment can say anything about candidate-generation quality. Every ordering conclusion is conditional on the matcher having already recalled the answer. This experiment measures the conditioning event.
decision_relevance.isolation_requirement: This does NOT modify the ordering corpus, its equality gate, or its result. Mixing candidate generation into that grid would destroy the single-variable isolation that makes the ordering result credible. The ordering gates stay exactly as they are; this experiment gets its own package, its own corpus, and its own subset gate.

lexical_miss.definition: A task whose query Q does not appear as a case-insensitive substring of the primary Memory's key or stored value, nor of any acceptable entry point's, while Q DOES appear literally in at least one distractor.
lexical_miss.why_the_distractor_requirement: Without it the literal matcher returns an empty candidate set and recall is 0 for a degenerate reason. Requiring a literal-matching distractor makes the literal arm return a non-empty but wrong candidate set, which is a real recall miss rather than an empty result.

miss_kinds.synonym: Q and the primary's surface form are different words for the same thing (query 'lease renewal', primary text 'tenancy extension').
miss_kinds.abbreviation: One side is an initialism or contraction of the other, in either direction (query 'time to live', primary text 'TTL').
miss_kinds.renamed_concept: The corpus records a rename; the primary uses the new name and the query uses the retired one (query 'worker pool', primary text 'executor group').
miss_kinds.morphological: Same stem, different surface form, so no substring match survives (query 'renewing leases', primary text 'lease renewal').

lexical_miss.kind_is_a_reported_stratum_not_a_gate: n=9 per kind is too small to gate on. Per-kind recall is reported with its n so a reader can see which capability drives any aggregate, and is explicitly not used to reach a verdict.

lexical_hit_control.definition: The 36 existing beads_ordering tasks, reused UNCHANGED from fixtures/beads_ordering/corpus.json.
lexical_hit_control.purpose: A generator that recovers lexical misses but loses Memories the literal matcher already found is not an improvement. Literal recall on this class is 1.0 by construction; the measurement is what the non-literal generators do on the same tasks.

construction_gates.when: at corpus freeze time, mechanically, with no model in the loop
construction_gates.miss_guarantee: for the primary and every acceptable entry point, assert Q.lower() not in (key + stored_value()).lower(); raise otherwise
construction_gates.hit_guarantee: assert Q.lower() in (key + stored_value()).lower() for at least one distractor; raise otherwise
construction_gates.no_incidental_matches: assert the literal candidate set over the frozen corpus is a SUBSET of the labelled set, so an unlabelled Memory never enters the candidate set by accident

runtime_gate.name: validate_lexical_miss_truth
runtime_gate.location: a NEW function in a NEW package (membench/lexical_recall/), never a relaxation of a shared symbol
runtime_gate.why_new: candidate_parity (membench/beads_ordering/client.py:114-145) is an arm-vs-arm gate that raises when two arms return different candidate sets, and it runs at runner.py:258 BEFORE the label check. An experiment that varies candidate generation makes differing candidate sets the expected outcome, so it needs a parallel seam. runner.py and density_linkage_evidence.py both call the shared symbol and must keep the strict behaviour.
assertions: set(literal_candidate_ids) is a SUBSET of the labelled set
the labelled set is unchanged from the frozen fixture

literal.what: Beads' shipped case-insensitive literal substring matcher over key and complete stored value
literal.how: bd --json memories <query> --experimental-order key --page-size all, cwd = seeded workspace
literal.binary: bd-memory-ordering-5877, pinned by sha256 in every result row; candidate generation in that binary is identical to stock (BM25F reorders the map memoryops.List already returned and cannot add or remove a candidate), so the ordering experiment and this one see the same candidate sets

fts.what: SQLite FTS5 over the same document text
fts.query_form: the query string split on non-alphanumerics, each term quoted, joined with OR
fts.why_or_not_phrase: a phrase query requires adjacency and would make the morphological and synonym kinds fail for a reason unrelated to the tokenizer. Bag-of-words OR is what a search index actually does. This choice materially affects recall and is therefore locked here rather than tuned later.
fts.index_built_by: this experiment, in process, over the frozen corpus; no FTS index exists over beads_ordering fixtures today

embedding.what: dense retrieval, exact in-process cosine, no ANN
embedding.model: nomic-embed-text served by the local Ollama daemon, 768 dimensions
embedding.why_this_model: local, offline, already present, and free, which satisfies the no-paid-API scope. It is not chosen for being the strongest available embedder, and the writeup must say so.
embedding.provenance: record the Ollama model digest and daemon version in the result
embedding.candidate_set: top-k by cosine over every Memory in the corpus; k is set by the endpoint's budget rule below, because a dense ranker has no natural cutoff

generators.identical_document_text: all three generators index exactly the string MemoryFixture.stored_value() produces, so no arm sees text another arm does not. This is the fairness control.

endpoint.primary: recall of primary_relevant in the generator's candidate set at matched-k, averaged over tasks with equal weight, per generator, per class
endpoint.matched_k: k = the size of the LITERAL candidate set for that same task, so every generator spends the same candidate budget
endpoint.why_matched_k_is_primary: recall without a size control is gameable: a generator that returns the whole corpus scores 1.0. Matched-k holds the budget fixed at what the shipped matcher already costs.
secondary: recall@10, a fixed absolute budget, because matched-k varies across tasks
unbounded recall, which is reported as a ceiling and is expected to be 1.0 for the embedding arm by definition
useful recall at matched-k, where a hit is the primary OR any acceptable entry point
candidate-set size actually returned by each generator

G1_recovery.statistic: primary recall@matched-k on the lexical_miss class, per non-literal generator
G1_recovery.note: the literal arm's recall on this class is 0 by construction. That is the definition of the class, not a finding, and must not be reported as a measured result.

G2_no_regression.statistic: primary recall@matched-k on the lexical_hit_control class, per non-literal generator
G2_no_regression.note: literal recall on this class is 1.0 by construction, so any value below 1.0 is a loss relative to what ships today.

G3_candidate_cost.statistic: median and p90 of |candidate set| / |literal candidate set| at the unbounded setting

gates.combined_recommendation: candidate generation earns its own arm in future ordering work if and only if some generator is both `recovers` under G1 and `preserves_literal_recall` under G2. Any other combination reports that the shipped literal matcher is not the bottleneck this experiment can demonstrate.

directional_predictions.why_recorded: a prediction written before measurement can be falsified; one written after cannot.
directional_predictions.fts_recovers_morphological: the porter tokenizer stems both surface forms to the same token, so FTS should recover the morphological kind and the literal matcher cannot
directional_predictions.embedding_recovers_synonym_and_renamed: these are the cases dense retrieval exists for
directional_predictions.abbreviation_is_hard_for_all_three: an initialism shares no stem with its expansion and is weakly represented in embedding space
directional_predictions.falsification_is_the_point: if FTS beats the embedding arm on synonyms, or the embedding arm fails the renamed-concept kind, that is the finding and it gets reported at the same prominence as a confirmation

counting_rule.primary: per-task recall, averaged over tasks with equal weight within a class
counting_rule.no_session_dimension: unlike mem-rj2mg there is no session structure here; every task is one deterministic retrieval per generator
counting_rule.repeats: the literal and FTS arms are deterministic and run once. The embedding arm runs 3 repeats to detect nondeterminism in the served model, and the writeup reports whether the 3 agreed.

zfc_split.mechanical: corpus construction gates, substring checks, FTS indexing and querying, cosine ranking, recall arithmetic, all deterministic
zfc_split.model: authoring the synonym, abbreviation, renamed-concept, and morphological pairs is semantic work and may use a model, but the OUTPUT is frozen into the fixture and every downstream check is mechanical
zfc_split.prohibited: any keyword or regex heuristic standing in for semantic judgment inside the measurement path, and any threshold tuned after seeing a recall number

analysis_plan.reporting: recall per generator per class, with per-kind strata and their n; candidate-set sizes; the three gate verdicts; and every deviation from this file with its direction of bias
analysis_plan.negative_result_handling: a result that no non-literal generator recovers the miss class is reported with the same prominence as a result that one does

privacy.published: the authored fixture, recall counts and fractions, candidate-set sizes, and gate verdicts
privacy.note: the corpus is authored, not derived from real work records, so there is no leak surface from the bead spine

threats_to_validity: the miss class is AUTHORED, so its difficulty is set by the author rather than observed. The recall numbers estimate performance on this constructed distribution, not on the queries agents actually issue. This is the mirror image of the defect the experiment exists to name and must be stated at the same prominence.

recall on the lexical_miss class being 0 for the literal arm is guaranteed by the construction gate. Reporting it as a measured result would repeat exactly the by-construction error this bead was filed against.
the corpus is synthetic and small relative to a real store, and the 500 generic notes are homogeneous in a way real notes are not
the embedding arm is pinned to one small local model chosen for being free and offline; a stronger embedder could change G1 in either direction and the result generalizes to this model only
matched-k favours the literal arm when its candidate set is small; unbounded recall and recall@10 are reported alongside precisely so that a reader can see the effect of the budget rule
the four miss kinds are not equally represented in real usage and the aggregate weights them equally, which is a choice, not a measurement
